label: Edison's tinfoil phonograph
detail: The first machine to record and play back sound; patent application filed December 24, 1877.

label: Berliner patents the gramophone
detail: Flat, double-sided discs with spiral grooves, cheaper to mass-produce than cylinders.

label: Commercial shellac 78s begin
detail: Shellac discs are produced commercially from 1897 until the late 1950s.

label: Edison switches to discs
detail: Edison announces the Edison Disc Phonograph, conceding the public prefers discs; cylinders continue until 1929.

label: Scully builds a lathe
detail: John J. Scully builds a weight-driven disc lathe.

label: Neumann AM31
detail: Neumann's first lathe, the AM31, arrives.

label: Cage uses records as an instrument
detail: John Cage's Imaginary Landscape No. 1 uses records switched between speeds.

label: Ortofon cutter head
detail: Ortofon makes its first moving-coil cutter head.

label: US press-parts supplier starts out
detail: Record Products of America begins supplying the record industry; it later sells parts for legacy presses.

label: The hot stylus
detail: William S. Bachman at Columbia develops the heated cutting stylus.

label: Columbia unveils the LP
detail: Announced at the Waldorf Astoria in New York; the Library of Congress gives June 21, other sources June 18.

label: RCA Victor introduces the 45
detail: A 7-inch 45 rpm single with a large center hole, the day after Columbia announced a 7-inch 33 1/3 single.

label: Variable pitch at Scully
detail: Per Wikipedia, Scully introduces variable pitch, automated in 1955.

label: The war of the speeds ends in a split
detail: RCA issues LPs in April and Columbia issues 45s in August: LP for albums, 45 for singles.

label: First record pressed at Loděnice
detail: The state-run Gramofonové závody near Prague, later GZ Media, presses its first record.

label: First record pressed at Lodenice
detail: The plant that became GZ Media, later described as the world's largest, presses its first record.

label: RIAA curve standardized
detail: The RIAA equalization curve replaces a mix of competing EQs, after the 1953 NARTB standard.

label: RIAA curve approved
detail: The RIAA Technical Committee approves one US playback equalization standard, still in use.

label: 45/45 stereo cutter head
detail: Per Wikipedia, Western Electric/Westrex demonstrates the first commercial 45/45 stereo cutter head.

label: Stereo standard adopted
detail: The RIAA adopts the Westrex 45/45 single-groove stereo system as the US standard.

label: 45/45 becomes the US stereo standard
detail: The Record Industry Association of America adopts the Westrex 45/45 stereo disc system as the American standard.

label: Capitol's IAM triangle
detail: Capitol's Scranton plant marks records with IAM in a triangle, roughly 1963 to 1973.

label: IEC 98 published
detail: The IEC disc recording standard that includes the RIAA curve is first published.

label: RCA record-wear study
detail: Woodward and colleagues at RCA publish an electron-microscope study of groove wear in JAES.

label: Porky starts cutting
detail: George Peckham starts as a cutting engineer at Apple in London.

label: Neumann VMS 70
detail: Neumann's VMS 70, which Pspatial Audio calls the world's most popular recording lathe.

label: Rounder Records founded in Somerville
detail: Bill Nowlin, Ken Irwin and Marian Leighton Levy start the roots label in an apartment.

label: Technics SL-1200 launched
detail: Matsushita launches the direct-drive SL-1200 under the Technics brand.

label: Scratching discovered (dates disputed)
detail: KEXP dates Grand Wizzard Theodore's discovery of scratching to 1975; other sources say 1977, the early 1980s or the early 1970s.

label: IEC adds a fourth time constant
detail: The IEC adds a 7950 microsecond infrasonic roll-off to the RIAA curve.

label: Peak plastic for US recorded music
detail: The US recording industry uses an estimated 58 million kg of plastic (academic estimate).

label: SL-1200MK2
detail: Technics releases the MK2, which it bills as the first turntable developed for discos.

label: Neumann VMS 80
detail: Neumann's last lathe line, the first without the traditional bed, with DC servo motors.

label: DMM arrives
detail: Teldec and Neumann's Direct Metal Mastering spreads in the early 1980s, cutting straight into copper.

label: Cassettes pass LPs
detail: Cassettes take 47.8% of US dollar value against 44.6% for LPs and EPs.

label: DMC championships begin
detail: The DMC World DJ Championships start.

label: Last VMS-82 DMM lathe
detail: The last Neumann VMS-82 DMM lathe is assembled in Berlin.

label: 'Turntablism' coined
detail: DJ Babu of the Beat Junkies coins the word turntablism.

label: Discogs launches
detail: Kevin Lewandowski starts Discogs.

label: Final Scratch released
detail: Stanton's Final Scratch, the first DVS software sold publicly per Wikipedia, comes out late in the year.

label: Serato Scratch Live
detail: Serato Scratch Live is released with Rane.

label: US loses its last DMM room
detail: Per Wikipedia, the last public DMM facility in the US closes.

label: Last US DMM room closes
detail: Per Wikipedia, the US loses its last DMM facility; a Discogs profile lists DMM cutting at Masterdisk, so this is disputed.

label: US vinyl hits bottom
detail: RIAA LP and EP shipments fall to about 900,000 (SoundScan's low, 857,000 albums, came in 2005).

label: First Record Store Day
detail: Conceived in September 2007 and first held in April 2008.

label: First Record Store Day
detail: The first official Record Store Day, after a 2007 gathering of US shop owners.

label: Black Friday RSD
detail: Record Store Day adds a Black Friday edition.

label: SL-1200 discontinued
detail: Panasonic announces the end of Technics analog turntables.

label: DMC allows DVS
detail: The DMC championships begin permitting vinyl-emulation systems.

label: 40 vinyl manufacturers counted worldwide
detail: The Vinyl Factory counts 40 manufacturers, with the US and Europe home to more than 80% (reported).

label: Thai supplier reported at up to 90% of record PVC
detail: FACT reports Thai Plastic & Chemicals supplies up to 90% of record compound; the last US supplier closed in the mid-2000s.

label: $790,000 White Album
detail: Ringo Starr's White Album No. 0000001 sells at Julien's, Los Angeles, the Guinness record for a vinyl record at auction.

label: SL-1200 returns
detail: The SL-1200G and limited SL-1200GAE are announced at CES and ship in April and October.

label: New presses arrive
detail: Viryl's WarmTone and Newbilt's Finebilt-based presses appear, among the first new presses in decades.

label: Vinyl Brazil announced
detail: A planned São Paulo plant would join Polysom, then Latin America's only plant.

label: Third Man Pressing runs Newbilt presses in Detroit
detail: The plant bought eight of the first ten Newbilt machines and expected about 5,000 records a shift.

label: Steamless press reported
detail: Viryl's steamless module heats mold water electrically to 285 F, removing the gas boiler.

label: US vinyl revenue passes CD
detail: $626 million against $483 million, the first time since 1986 (RIAA).

label: RSD Drops
detail: Record Store Day is split into three Drops.

label: Lacquer factory fire
detail: A fire destroys the Apollo Masters lacquer factory in Banning, California, leaving MDC in Japan as the sole lacquer maker.

label: Apollo Masters lacquer plant burns
detail: Fire destroys the only US lacquer maker, estimated at 70-85% of world supply (reported).

label: Lead times of three months to a year
detail: Mixmag reports long waits, Adele's 30 at over 500,000 vinyl copies, and capacity of about 160 million against demand of about 400 million a year.

label: US vinyl passes CD in units
detail: 41 million vinyl units against 33 million CDs, the first time since 1987 (RIAA).

label: Lead times hit 9-12 months
detail: GRAMMY.com reports industry-wide waits, against 4-6 weeks in 2018.

label: Agnew Type 612
detail: A new disk mastering lathe is unveiled at the International Disk Recording and Mastering Convention.

label: BioVinyl launched
detail: optimal media and PlastChem launch a bio-attributed PVC record.

label: EcoRecord launched
detail: Sonopress and Warner Music launch an injection-molded PET record; energy and sound claims are the maker's.

label: Burlington Record Plant sold, set to move
detail: Equal Vision Records buys the plant, planning a July 2024 move to Albany, New York.

label: India presses its first record in decades
detail: A plant in Navi Mumbai presses its first record, one of several new entrants reported in 2024.

label: US vinyl tops $1 billion
detail: $1,042.9 million on 46.8 million units, the 19th straight year of growth (RIAA).

label: Discogs collection record
detail: Discogs users add a record 114.2 million items to their collections (official, company figure).

label: Backlog about three months
detail: Hypebot reports the typical plant backlog at about three months.

label: The Life of a Showgirl released
detail: It sells 1.2 million vinyl copies on day one in the US, per Luminate.

label: US vinyl passes $1 billion
detail: The RIAA's 2025 report shows vinyl revenue over $1 billion for the first time since 1983.

label: $25,000 White Stripes 7-inch
detail: The White Stripes' "Lafayette Blues" sells for $25,000 on Discogs (reported).

label: APC-2 lathe
detail: MusicTech reports the Teenage Engineering and SUPERSENSE APC-2, a 104 kg made-to-order lathe.

label: RIAA mid-year 2026
detail: US vinyl up 17.7% and CDs up 58.6% in the first half of 2026.
